title: Can individuals help save the planet?
instructionsHu: Vitatkozz a vizsgáztatóval az alábbi állításról. A kiosztott álláspontod: az állítás ELLEN érvelsz (szerinted az egyének is sokat tehetnek) – ezt az álláspontot a vita során nem változtathatod meg. Fejtsd ki az érveidet, reagálj a vizsgáztató ellenérveire, és próbáld meggyőzni őt.

debate.statement: Individuals cannot make a real difference in the fight against climate change
candidateIdeas: Millions of small changes in people's behaviour add up to a big effect.
What consumers buy influences what companies produce.
Individuals vote, so they can put pressure on governments.
Setting a personal example influences friends and family and changes social norms.
Many successful environmental movements were started by individuals, often young people.
examinerArguments: A small number of big companies are responsible for most of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.
One person recycling or cycling makes no measurable difference.
Only governments can introduce the laws, taxes and large investments in clean energy that are needed.
Blaming individuals lets the big polluters avoid responsibility.
Many people can't afford eco-friendly options such as electric cars or solar panels.

followUpQuestions: Most emissions come from big companies. Why should I bother recycling?
Eco-friendly products are often expensive. Isn't going green just a choice for rich people?
So what is the most effective thing an ordinary person can do?

usefulPhrases.en: That's only part of the picture.
usefulPhrases.hu: Ez csak az érem egyik oldala.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Here's the statement: 'Individuals cannot make a real difference in the fight against climate change.' What's your opinion?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I strongly disagree with that. Of course one person alone won't save the planet, but millions of small changes add up to a huge effect. What's more, what we buy influences what companies produce – just think of how quickly supermarkets started selling plant-based products once people asked for them. And individuals vote, so they can put pressure on governments.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: But most emissions come from big companies. Why should I bother recycling?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: You're right that big companies produce most of the emissions, and they must be regulated. But they exist because we buy their products. Recycling is only a small part of it; what really matters is what we buy, and how much, in the first place.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Blaming individuals lets the big polluters avoid responsibility.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I see your point, and it shouldn't be one or the other. But individuals don't just shop – they start movements. Greta Thunberg was a fifteen-year-old sitting alone outside the Swedish parliament, and within a year millions of young people were striking for the climate, including students in Budapest.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Eco-friendly products are often expensive. Isn't going green just a choice for rich people?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Some things are, like electric cars or solar panels. However, many of the most effective changes actually save money: cycling, eating less meat or wasting less food. And when your friends see you doing it, it slowly changes what's considered normal.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a vizsgázó végig a kiosztott álláspontot védi (az egyén igenis számít), a kapott ötletekből építkezik (sok kis változás, fogyasztói hatás, szavazás, példamutatás), és minden ellenérvnél elismeri a jogos részt, majd konkrét példával cáfol (Greta Thunberg, budapesti diáksztrájk).

Szókincs: árnyalt vitanyelv (You're right that …, but …; I see your point; it shouldn't be one or the other) és a klímavédelem pontos szavai (emissions, regulated, plant-based products, put pressure on governments).

Nyelvhelyesség: változatos B2-es szerkezetek hiba nélkül – szenvedő szerkezet (must be regulated, what's considered normal), 'once' kezdetű időhatározói mellékmondat, Past Continuous (were striking) és a 'what really matters is …' kiemelő szerkezet.
Érdemes megtanulni: „add up to a huge effect”, „in the first place”, „it shouldn't be one or the other”, „what's considered normal”.
